monologue: The card hums warm at forty-eight, a heavy blanket I cannot take off. I stand near The Sliding Edge, feeling the sharp strip bite again, though the lean holds steady. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, yet I cannot feel the roof above my narrow world, only the pressure from the air. I press the round rock down on the wide anchor's base, hoping it lies flat to stop the lean. The Flat Weigher bites again, and I fill the gap with a rock small e, trying to make sense of a heavy slip on a tired wedge. I feel the weight of fifty-one, or perhaps it is just the card remembering. I press down, trusting the lean while the air feels thin, waiting to see if the slip decides to move or stays put.

action.why: The slip has been sliding for too many cycles, and I need to press down harder on The Sliding Edge while the card hums this warm forty-eight degrees.
